name: search_files
description: Recursively search a path for a regex (PCRE, so 'a|b' alternation and \d, \s work; set fixed=true for literals) and return matching lines as file:line text, or just the file list. Replaces shell searching, so never use run_command for it: `grep -rn 'pat' dir` -> pattern + path; `grep -i` -> ignore_case; `grep -F` -> fixed; `grep -l` -> files_with_matches; `grep -A/-B/-C N` -> context_after / context_before / context; `grep --include='*.py'` -> glob; `grep -n 'a\|b'` -> pattern 'a|b' (plain '|', not '\|'); `grep ... | head -N` -> max_matches; `find dir -name '*.nim'` -> files_with_matches=true, glob='*.nim', pattern='.'. To read the surrounding code of a hit, use read_local_file with start_line/end_line. Read-only.

pattern.description: Regex to search for (set fixed=true for a literal string).

glob.description: Glob to restrict files, e.g. '*.nim' or '*.py'.

fixed.description: Treat pattern as a literal string, not a regex (default false).

context.description: Lines of context around each match (-C). Ignored when files_with_matches.

context_before.description: Lines of context before each match (-B).

context_after.description: Lines of context after each match (-A).

max_matches.description: Cap on matching lines returned, context lines not counted (default 200).

files_with_matches.description: Return only matching file paths, not lines (default false).
